items.q: What do we forget when we treat body language as communication?
items.a: We already judge others from thin slices (30 silent seconds of a doctor; **1 second** of a candidate's face). The forgotten audience is **yourself**. Nonverbals change **your** thoughts, feelings, and next five minutes.

items.q: What is the power nonverbal, in one contrast?
items.a: **Expand vs collapse.** Open, take space, chin up — even people born blind throw the pride V at the finish line. Wrap, hunch, protect the neck when you feel small. In a room, people **complement** rather than mirror: one person's expand shrinks the other.

items.q: Where should you power-pose — and where must you not?
items.a: **Bathroom, elevator, closed door.** Not in the interview. Media heard 'do Wonder Woman at the table.' Cuddy: this is you talking to **yourself**. Two minutes before the evaluative room.

items.q: What did the interview study actually move?
items.a: Blind coders wanted to **hire the high-power posers**. Speech structure, quality, qualifications **did not move**. **Presence** did — they showed up as themselves, 'no residue.' Treat the 2012 hormone percentages as the talk's claim, not settled physiology.

items.q: Why does Cuddy reject 'fake it till you make it'?
items.a: Make-it still leaves you arriving as a **fraud**. She wants **become-it**: do every talk until you notice you are doing it. After the wreck, IQ down two SDs, 'gifted' gone: **I'm not supposed to be here.** Years later a silent student said the same sentence — and Cuddy no longer felt it.
People with **no resources, no tech, no status**. They need a body, privacy, and two minutes. Tiny tweaks → leave the room feeling you **showed who you are**, not that you hid.
